---

`camtrapReport` turns camera-trap data in [Camtrap DP](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/)
format into reproducible data-quality assessments and ecological reports. It
combines data checks, ecological analyses, visualisations, and explanatory text
in a configurable workflow, helping researchers report consistently across
sites and surveys. The package produces two complementary outputs:

- **Data Status Check:** checks data completeness, consistency, annotations,
  and spatial and temporal coverage.
- **Ecological Report:** brings together selected analyses, figures, maps,
  tables, and explanatory text in a configurable report.

Reports are generated as HTML by default. PDF export is available for
ecological reports where supported by the selected modules and local setup.
You can work directly in R or use the optional graphical interface.

  <img src="vignettes/figures/package-architecture.png"

## Available analyses

`camtrapReport` provides modules for describing sampling, summarising species
observations, and exploring ecological patterns. The table lists available
modules; the analyses included in a particular report depend on its selected
[profile](#profiles), data, and requirements.

| Analysis | Available modules | Main inputs or considerations |
|---|---|---|
| Study and sampling | `introduction`, `methods`, `study_area`, `sampling`, `location`, `effort`, `image_processing`, `data_processing` | Metadata, deployments, and optional study-area boundary |
| Captures and trends | `results`, `captures`, `abundance_trends` | Observations and sampling effort; capture rates are not density estimates |
| Population density (REM) | `population_density`, `model_parameters`, `population_densities` | Species-specific REM inputs and assumptions |
| Activity and community patterns | `activity_patterns`, `richness`, `co_occurrence`, `species_accumulation` | Species records, timestamps, and sufficient observations |
| Spatial and habitat analyses | `spatial_density`, `habitat_preferences` | Camera locations and, where relevant, habitat data |
| Supporting sections | `acknowledgements`, `appendix`, `References` | Supplementary information and citations |

Data-status modules assess spatial and temporal information, availability,
validation, annotations, and observation types. Some ecological analyses need
additional data or optional R packages. See the [Ecological Report guide](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/ecological-report.html)
for interpretation and requirements.

## Installation

`camtrapReport` requires R 4.1.0 or later. Install the development version
from GitHub:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pak")
}
pak::pkg_install("spatialecology/camtrapReport")
```

Some analytical modules require optional R packages. If a selected module
reports a missing dependency, install the required package. Alternatively,
`camtrapReport::install_all()` checks dependencies for bundled and registered
modules, but may install many packages. The core workflow does not require
launching the graphical interface.

## Prepare your data

Start with a [Camtrap DP](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/) dataset containing its
metadata and related deployment, media, and observation tables. If your data
are in another format, prepare and validate a Camtrap DP dataset first; the
[`camtrapdp` package](https://inbo.github.io/camtrapdp/) provides tools and
examples for this step.

`camData()` accepts an extracted Camtrap DP directory or ZIP archive. Habitat
information and a study-area boundary are optional. If a study-area boundary changes between surveys, account for that when
interpreting spatial results. See the [Data Status Check guide](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/data-status-report.html)
and `?camData` for input details.

`camData()` can save processed files alongside the source dataset. The example
below works on a temporary copy so the bundled data remain unchanged. If you
correct the source CSV or JSON files, reload with `update = TRUE` before
rerunning reports to refresh the processed object.

## Quick start

This example uses a compact Camtrap DP dataset derived from **GMU8_LEUVEN**,
with bundled habitat information and a study-area boundary.

```{r quick-start}
library(camtrapReport)

example_root <- tempfile("camtrapReport-example-")

dir.create(
  example_root,
  recursive = TRUE
)

copied <- file.copy(
  from = system.file(
    "external",
    "dataset",
    package = "camtrapReport",
    mustWork = TRUE
  ),
  to = example_root,
  recursive = TRUE,
  copy.mode = FALSE
)

habitat <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file(
    "external",
    "habitat",
    "habitat.csv",
    package = "camtrapReport",
    mustWork = TRUE
  )
)

study_area <- system.file(
  "external",
  "study_area",
  "study_area.shp",
  package = "camtrapReport",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
```

```{r validate-example-data, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(copied),
  dir.exists(file.path(example_root, "dataset"))
)
```

```{r create-camreport-object, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
cm <- camData(
  data = file.path(example_root, "dataset"),
  habitat = habitat,
  study_area = study_area,
  update = TRUE
)
```

```{r show-camreport-object}
cm
```

### 1. Check your data

Run `status()` to review completeness, consistency, and spatial and temporal
coverage before interpreting ecological results.

```{r generate-data-status, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
status_file <- status(cm, view = FALSE)
```

[View an example Data Status Check](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/reports/DataStatusReport_example.html).
Review the findings, correct relevant issues in your source data, reload with
`camData(..., update = TRUE)`, and rerun `status()` as needed. Not every
warning necessarily means that a dataset is unusable; assess its relevance to
the intended analysis.

### 2. Generate an ecological report

Run `report()` to combine selected analyses, figures, tables, and explanatory
text in one report.

```{r generate-ecological-report, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
report_file <- report(cm, view = FALSE)
```

[View an example Ecological Report](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/reports/EcologicalReport_example.html).
Report content depends on the selected modules, input data, and installed
optional packages. The example output may therefore differ from reports made
with other datasets or settings. Set `view = TRUE` to open a generated report.

### 3. Choose report sections

```{r configure-report, eval=FALSE}
# See available section names
section_names()

# Choose a smaller ecological report
selected <- section_names(
  keep = c("introduction", "methods", "study_area", "sampling", "effort")
)
sections(cm, selected)

# Generate the configured report
report(cm, filename = "selected-report.html", view = FALSE)
```

For more control over module selection and report content, see the [Ecological Report](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/ecological-report.html)
and [Module management](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/modules.html)
guides. Report narratives come from the selected module definitions, including
text that may be filled using dataset metadata and analytical results. To edit
or replace that text, follow the module guide rather than editing generated
HTML files.

## Profiles

Camera-trap monitoring networks may follow the same data standard while using
different analytical methods, parameters, and reporting conventions.
**Analytical profiles** make these choices reusable across datasets, sites, and
repeated surveys. A profile selects and configures report modules for a
particular monitoring context.

For example, the **European Observatory of Wildlife (EOW)** profile uses
annual Random Encounter Model (REM) calculations with parameters estimated
separately for each species and sampling year, whereas the default profile
uses pooled parameters across years.

Explore the available profiles and inspect their selected modules:

```{r profile-report, eval=FALSE}
# Explore available profiles
profile_names(cm)

# Inspect the modules selected by the EOW profile
section_names(object = cm, profile = "EOW")

# Generate an ecological report using the EOW profile
report(
  cm,
  profile = "EOW",
  format = "pdf",
  filename = "EOW-report.pdf"
)
```


Networks and individual projects can also create and share their own profiles,
reusing analytical components while documenting distinct reporting workflows.
See the [Profiles guide](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/profiles.html)
for creating, editing, and sharing profiles.

A profile standardises selected methods and settings; it does not establish
that those methods are suitable for every dataset. Evaluate sampling design,
input requirements, and method-specific assumptions before interpreting results.
   
## Reproducibility and interpretation

A successful Data Status Check means that the implemented checks completed;
it does not establish the validity of every ecological analysis. Interpret
results in light of sampling design, effort, detectability, and method-specific
assumptions. Retain your source data, selected profile and modules, settings,
and software versions. Check reports for sensitive species locations before
sharing them.

The bundled example data are a reduced, relationship-preserving subset of the
[GMU8_LEUVEN dataset](https://doi.org/10.15468/4u3wm4), published by INBO
through GBIF. They are provided for demonstrations and tests, **not ecological
inference**. See the [example-data provenance](https://github.com/spatialecology/camtrapReport/blob/main/inst/external/README-Leuven-dataset.md).

## Documentation and support

- [Data Status Check](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/data-status-report.html)
- [Ecological Report](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/ecological-report.html)
- [Profiles](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/profiles.html)
- [Module management](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/modules.html)
- [Function reference](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/reference/index.html)
- [Issues and feature requests](https://github.com/spatialecology/camtrapReport/issues)

Related tools include [`camtrapdp`](https://inbo.github.io/camtrapdp/),
[`camtraptor`](https://inbo.github.io/camtraptor/),
[`camtrapR`](https://jniedballa.github.io/camtrapR/), and
[`ct`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ct). `camtrapReport` complements these tools by bringing data checks and
selected analyses together in configurable reports. Development and evaluation
have involved real-world camera-trap datasets and feedback from users;
see the [Resources page](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/resources.html).
